name: Just Breathe Normally (The Lumen Skin Recall)
creator: Original: Axiom Wellness Division PR feed; propagated by anonymous Shelf editors
description: During a live neural-feed product demonstration for Lumen Skin — a bioluminescent geneware cosmetic — the Axiom spokesperson Dreya Okonkwo-Fassbender began involuntarily pulsing bright orange across her entire face when her BCI registered elevated cortisol, a defect the product was supposed to suppress. Her whispered instruction to herself, 'just breathe normally,' was picked up by the broadcast mic and became the defining phrase for any situation where someone is visibly failing while insisting they are fine. The clip spread within six hours to every pirate feed on the Shelf before Axiom could scrub the official broadcast.
medium: neural feed clip (pirate rebroadcast); later preserved as physical thumb-chip artifact
cultural_impact: The phrase 'just breathe normally' entered daily speech as shorthand for catastrophic public composure failure, and is especially weaponized in political commentary; it permanently damaged Axiom Wellness's geneware credibility for three product cycles.
controversy: Axiom pursued aggressive takedown litigation for two years, which only amplified the clip's reach; the spokesperson Okonkwo-Fassbender later gave a single interview describing the experience as 'being eaten alive in real time' — that interview also went viral.
story_hooks: A character uses the phrase at exactly the wrong moment in a high-stakes negotiation with an Axiom representative who was present at the original broadcast.
Someone discovers that the 'defect' was not an accident — a whistleblower claims the cortisol-pulse response was a suppressed safety feature Axiom removed to cut costs.
A Shelf artist wants to track down Dreya Okonkwo-Fassbender to include her in a documentary about corporate bodies as involuntary performance art.
